The all-purpose flour is fundamental, providing the structural body that defines the biscotti. Eggs also carry much structural and binding function. Hazelnuts contribute strongly to the flavor and texture, defining the nutty character essential to the recipe. Orange zest and juice provide key citrus flavor notes that are characteristic of this biscotti variant. Baking soda and baking powder contribute to leavening, affecting texture noticeably. Olive oil acts as the fat component, affecting moisture and texture. Sugar is important for sweetness and flavor balance. Bittersweet chocolate is applied as a glaze, enhancing flavor but not defining the biscotti itself, so given a moderate score. Shortening is only used for melting with chocolate, acting as a medium for glazing, so it has a minor structural/flavor role. Salt is minor but contributes subtle seasoning.

Evaporated milk contributes to the batter's thickness and flavor, thus important but less so than flour. Vegetable oil is essential for frying and achieving the characteristic golden crust. Sugar, salt, and pepper provide seasoning, with salt and pepper slightly more important, but all are minor contributors compared to the main ingredients.

Pecorino romano cheese, olive oil, and garlic contribute clear flavors and richness, enhancing but not dominating the dish. Onion plays a moderate supporting role in the sauce development. Black pepper and salt are important seasonings but provide a minor supporting role rather than defining flavors.

Tomatoes and salt & pepper offer seasoning and subtle flavor adjustments (0.25 and 0.5).
